To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

intersectionality is a powerful tool for understanding how multiple forms of oppression and privilege intersect and interact, and that assemblage theory can be used to understand the ways in which people, objects, and ideas come together to form complex systems and relationships.

1) intersectionality and assemblages are two distinct and divergent genealogies; 2) intersectionality is a political project that has been successful in some realms of feminist knowledge production and organizing, but has been less successful in others; and 3) assemblages, while a less well-developed concept, may offer some of the same benefits of intersectionality, but also offer some new possibilities for feminist theorizing and organizing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether the intersectionality framework can be usefully deployed as a tool for feminist knowledge production.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
intersectionality has become a dominant paradigm for feminist and queer theory, while assemblage has been a less dominant paradigm for feminist theory.
the politics and utility of intersectionality and assemblages are different, but they are not necessarily in conflict.
the politics of intersectionality are not necessarily the politics of assemblages and vice versa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
intersectionality is a political tool, a method, a way of seeing and being, and a way of doing, while assemblage is a way of thinking.
intersectionality is a tool for political analysis, while assemblage is a tool for social transformation.
intersectionality is an analytic and assemblage a political concept, but that both are useful for understanding the world and making it better.
The main takeaway from our work is that
intersectionality and assemblages, as analytics, have distinct and divergent histories and trajectories.
assemblage is an important supplement to intersectionality in the realm of political intervention.
the political possibilities for assemblage are as varied as the possibilities of intersectionality.
